The amended FY2025 10-K/A corrected the description of Client segment revenue growth drivers [1][2]. The original FY2025 10-K attributed the growth to "a 31% increase in unit shipments of processors and a 15% increase in average selling price of processors [1]". The amended 10-K/A instead attributes the growth to "a 15% increase in unit shipments of processors and a 31% increase in average selling price of processors", swapping the two percentages [2].

The amended 10-K/A reports Client net revenue of $10.6 billion in 2025, up from $7.1 billion in 2024, with total Client and Gaming net revenue of $14.6 billion in 2025, up 51% from $9.6 billion in 2024 [2]. The amended filing also reports Client and Gaming operating income of $2.9 billion in 2025, compared to $1.2 billion in 2024 [2].

The amended 10-K/A states that research and development expenses were $8.1 billion in 2025, increasing by $1.6 billion, or 25%, compared to $6.5 billion in 2024 [3]. The amended filing describes an October 2025 agreement with OpenAI to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, with AMD issuing a warrant to purchase up to 160 million shares at an exercise price of $0.01 per share [4].
